title: Adaptive Escalation Gateway for Signal Degradation
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem statement: our current incident pipeline treats every alert as a static escalation path. When metrics/trace signals degrade (increased tail latency, KV-cache miss storms, or sudden error spikes) we frequently over-escalate or under-provide context, causing noisy PD pages and slow TTR. Goals: (1) Dynamically determine escalation tier based on signal fidelity and cross-platform evidence; (2) attach compact evidence bundles (trace snippets, relevant logs, latency heatmap) into Slack and PD payloads; (3) inject context-aware runbook snippets and suggested remediation commands; (4) provide an automated severity ramp and graceful fallback routing to a secondary on-call pool when primary capacity is saturated.
acceptance_criteria: - PD pages contain an "evidence bundle" link that opens a curated trace+log snippet with annotated suspect spans. - Slack incident thread receives an auto-generated compact runbook with 2-3 prioritized next actions and a link to the full runbook. - Escalation tier is adjusted automatically when synthetic monitors or trace samplers indicate >80% degradation confidence; manual override still available. - If escalation fails (no ack within configured window), gateway reroutes to secondary pool and appends an incident seed to our postmortem automation queue. - Unit/integration tests cover evidence assembly, PD/Slack payload generation, and backoff/reroute behavior. - Performance: decision latency <200ms for incoming alert metadata payloads. - Feature guarded behind feature-flag and rolloutable per-organization.
implementation_notes: Design: gateway runs as a small stateless service in the ops namespace that subscribes to the telemetry event bus (trace-alerts + metrics-alerts). It enriches events via the trace-indexer (sampled spans) and logs-query adapter, then runs a compact heuristic model to compute confidence and recommended tier. Evidence bundling uses our existing KV cache snapshotter and a new trace-snippet serializer (gzip+base64) to keep PD payload sizes small. Slack attachments use block-kit with a compact summary first and 'Show evidence' link to the internal viewer.
rollout_plan: 1) Deploy behind a feature flag to staging and test with synthetic alert streams. 2) Canary to 5 internal teams for 2 weeks; monitor false positive/negative rates and PD noise metrics. 3) Gradual ramp to 25% of customer-facing alerts with telemetry guardrails. 4) Full rollout after SLI verification and one post-canary retrospective.
risks_and_mitigations: - Risk: excessive PD pages if confidence model misfires. Mitigation: start conservative thresholds and create a suppression window metric. - Risk: sensitive data leak in evidence bundles. Mitigation: scrub PII by default and test KMS access for evidence storage links. - Risk: gateway introduces latency in alerting path. Mitigation: keep decision path <200ms and fall back to pass-through if overloaded.
qa_steps: - Generate synthetic latency spike events and verify PD + Slack payloads. - Validate evidence bundle viewer shows trace snippets and links to full trace. - Force primary on-call to not ack and confirm reroute to secondary pool. - Run fuzz tests with malformed telemetry to confirm gateway fails open (no escalation blocking).
telemetry_queries_and_dashboards: - Latency spike detector query: service.latency.p99 > baseline * 3 over 5m. - Evidence bundle creation rate and average size. - PD page noise: alerts/page ratio and ack latency. - Gateway decision latency histogram. - Dashboard: 'Adaptive Escalation — Health' with success/fallback counts and per-org error rate.
